title: Thiomersal as a vaccine preservative = L’utilisation du thiomersal comme conservateur pour vaccins

sections.title: Front matter

summary.text: A bilingual Weekly Epidemiological Record item on thiomersal as a vaccine preservative, in which WHO supports the 1999 US statement on phasing it out while urging continued use of current children's vaccines that contain it. It explains thiomersal's long use against contamination of multidose vials and that no serious adverse events have been attributed to it. It reviews what is known about ethylmercury and methylmercury toxicity and promotes a preservative-free hepatitis B device for newborns. The French portion, with garbled accented characters, discusses the costs and supply problems of removing thiomersal, especially for developing countries.

sections.title: Summary

summary.text: An English summary stating that thiomersal carries a theoretical low risk to infants, far outweighed by the risks of vaccine-preventable disease and contaminated vials, and outlining short- and long-term plans to reduce it in vaccines.

sections.extract: Thiomersal poses a theoretical low risk of neurodevelopmental toxic- ity in infants. The known risk of morbidity and mortality from vaccine- preventable diseases and of contaminated multidose vaccine vials far outweigh any potential risk posed by thiomersal. sections.title: Résumé

summary.text: The French summary on thiomersal, followed by English and French text on combination vaccines and preservative-free delivery systems as ways to reduce preservative use. It notes that licensing a vaccine with a new preservative could take over a year. It ends with standard notices on reporting under the International Health Regulations and on the presentation of geographical areas, and parts of the French text have garbled accented characters.
